content: Cobicistat is a medication used to enhance (boost) the levels of certain HIV protease inhibitors, such as atazanavir and darunavir, in the body. It is not a cure for HIV infection. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, it is essential to continue taking all prescribed HIV medications exactly as directed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity, and avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may come into contact with blood or other body fluids. This medication should be taken by mouth with food, usually once daily, as prescribed by your doctor. It is crucial to adhere to the prescribed schedule and not to stop taking this medication or other HIV medications without consulting your doctor, even for a short time. The medication works best when its levels in the body are kept constant, so it should be taken at evenly spaced intervals. Nausea may occur as a side effect. However, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of these infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen shortly after starting HIV treatment or even months later. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. Before taking cobicistat, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cobicistat is not recommended for use during pregnancy, as it may not work effectively in pregnant women. If you become pregnant or suspect you may be pregnant, inform your doctor immediately. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) advises against breastfeeding for HIV-infected mothers due to the risk of postnatal transmission of HIV. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Cobicistat can slow the removal of other medications from the body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Similarly, other medications can influence how cobicistat is metabolized. Examples include drugs used to treat seizures (e.g., carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin), certain HIV medications (e.g., efavirenz, etravirine), and rifampin. This medication may also reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods, such as pills, patches, or rings, increasing the risk of pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use additional reliable backup birth control methods while taking this medication. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 12 hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication in its original container at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Cobicistat is generally well-tolerated, but it is important to monitor for potential side effects and drug interactions. Regular medical and laboratory tests, such as kidney function assessments, may be required before and during treatment. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
